title: ETFs, index funds, fund of funds and international funds
objectives: Differentiate ETFs, index funds and funds of funds.
Explain tracking error, tracking difference and international fund limits.
body_md:
## Passive and fund-of-funds

| Product | How it works |
|---|---|
| **Index fund** | Open-ended, copies an index, bought at NAV |
| **ETF** | Units trade on an **exchange** at market price through a demat account; AMC deals in **creation units** with authorised participants |
| **Fund of funds (FoF)** | Invests in other schemes: the investor bears **two layers of cost** (check the FoF expense limit) |
| **Gold fund / gold ETF** | Tracks the domestic gold price |
| **International fund** | Invests in overseas securities, directly or through a FoF |

## Passive measures

- **Tracking error:** standard deviation of the difference between fund and index returns.
- **Tracking difference:** the actual return gap over a period, mostly the cost.
- ETF price can trade at a small premium or discount to its **iNAV**; use limit orders on liquid ETFs.

## International funds

Overseas investment by funds is capped under **industry-wide and per-AMC limits**, so schemes may pause fresh subscriptions when a limit is reached. Currency moves add to the return and the risk. Tax follows the equity-oriented test: check the taxation lesson for the current rule.

## Fit

Passive funds suit low-cost core holdings; active funds are justified only when the extra cost buys something.

> **Exam tip:** ETFs trade on an exchange; index funds do not. FoFs add a second layer of expense.
example: An index fund returns 11.6% while its index returns 11.9%: the tracking difference is 0.3 percentage points, close to its expense ratio.
say: An ETF needs a demat account and trades through the day.
A fund of funds carries costs at two levels.
never: ETFs always trade exactly at NAV.

check.q: Which product is bought and sold on a stock exchange?

o: Volatility of the gap between fund and index returns
check.why: It is the standard deviation of the return difference.

check.q: A fund of funds is expensive mainly because:
check.why: Underlying and FoF costs both apply.
